svg.title: Data Agent on DuckDB
svg.text: Six layers: scheduling · semantic · context · governance · compute · storage — in-process DuckDB reads S3 Tables in place, Lake Formation is the policy authority, non-lake sources arrive as owner-bound handles
Lake on S3 — one access path · Lake Formation authority
Non-lake sources — through AgentCore Gateway, landed as handles
Claude Code / Kiro · stdio proxy mints the ID token
caller JWT in · Cedar per persona · source credential out
Redshift · Aurora PostgreSQL · fixed read-only tools
shape · stub · table map · cost gate

g.text: 3LO / OBO / IdC per user · rows → owner-bound _r_<n>

svg.text: user signs in at the IdP; AgentCore Identity validates the
JWT at the service entry — only verified requests reach a
Claims → role, session bound to its owner
verified {tenant, role, sub} map to a role policy; 1 session
= 1 microVM = 1 engine, and an owner change resets engine,
the agent calls Amazon Bedrock (Claude): DESCRIBE, sample,
fix errors, aggregate — engine feedback returns in
the governance layer rewrites every statement under the role
policy — RLS predicate, column exclusion, raw-path denial,
no shadowing, unparseable means refused, no policy means
Lake Formation is the authority, the rewrite is the enforcement point
row/column authorization can never be pushed into object
storage, so under Lake Formation's distributed-enforcement
model the data-cell filters are compiled into the rewrite
and applied in-process, fail-closed; a failed policy fetch
means deny-all (target state; the env policy is
today's authority and stays the no-LF fallback and the lower
One access path, data stays on S3
S3 Tables managed Iceberg over the Iceberg REST endpoint — 1
REST GET + 7 GETs, no LIST; the account's own exports are
curated into the same table by the same engine (three
compatibility legs remain in code, not in the design)
results → _r_ handles + schema summary, never truncation;
history → stubs at those handles; table map generated from
the engine catalog; the cost gate demands a partition filter
and expands literals to explicit paths; budgets
second runtime, same image, MCP protocol, same JWT
authorizer; five read-only tools enter the same pipeline
with the token's identity (a Gateway hop cannot forward the
user's JWT to a Runtime target — measured)
Non-lake sources: three permission levels, no credential in the agent
agent level = the Gateway's target list; persona level =
Cedar policy plus the policy's own source allowlist,
fail-closed if either is missing; user level = 3LO /
on-behalf-of / IdC propagation so the source authorizes the
real user, with 2LO an explicit audited degradation; rows
land as owner-bound _r_<n> handles and JOIN the lake

Dashed Lake Formation flows and the curation arrow are target state; all else is shipped and measured — the 2025-02-21 slice counts 1,226,888 through every access method and on DuckDB 2.0-alpha; governance matrix 191/191 over six paths. docs/eval-results.md
